family_diagnostics.where_to_look_first: Ask whether the plant is woody and opposite-leaved, then confirm a long 2-valved capsule with many flat winged seeds.
family_diagnostics.habit: Trees, shrubs or woody vines; local anchors are woody climbers.
family_diagnostics.flower: Showy tubular zygomorphic flowers, commonly with 4 didynamous stamens plus a staminode.
family_diagnostics.fruit: Usually a long 2-valved capsule with numerous flattened winged seeds.
family_diagnostics.field_tip: Opposite compound leaves are NOT universal: Bignonia has paired leaflets plus a terminal adhesive tendril; Campsis has pinnate leaves and stem rootlets; Catalpa has broad simple leaves; Chilopsis has narrow simple leaves that may be alternate; Tecoma has pinnate leaves. Confirm a mature capsule and seeds rather than flower color.
look_here_first_sequence: Inspect a complete leaf and its node: simple vs compound and leaf attachment; opposite leaves are common but Chilopsis can be alternate.
On climbing vines inspect the actual attachment: Campsis uses stem-borne aerial rootlets; Bignonia uses a leaf-derived tendril with adhesive tips.
Inspect a flower for a fused bilateral corolla and usually four didynamous stamens (two long, two short); a fifth staminode is not guaranteed.
Confirm a mature dry two-valved capsule with many flattened winged or fringed seeds; contrast Oleaceae samara/drupes and Paulownia's ovoid capsule.

visual_lesson.teaching_order: whole plant → high-value structure → reproductive confirmation → tie-breaker
visual_lesson.intro: Trumpet flowers get attention, but the woody vine and the long capsule full of winged seeds are what really lock Bignoniaceae in.

steps.title: 1 · See the whole trumpet-vine plan
steps.look_for: Woody climbing habit, opposite pinnately compound leaves, and large tubular flowers.
steps.why_it_matters: Combines the strongest vegetative and floral family cues.

steps.title: 2 · Ignore flower color and find the capsule
steps.look_for: A long dry capsule that splits into two valves.
steps.why_it_matters: The fruit is more diagnostic than an orange trumpet flower.

steps.title: 3 · Look at the seeds
steps.look_for: Many thin flattened seeds with broad papery wings.
steps.why_it_matters: Winged seeds inside a long woody-vine capsule strongly support Bignoniaceae.

steps.title: 4 · Check the flower interior
steps.look_for: Four fertile stamens plus a reduced fifth stamen/staminode.
steps.why_it_matters: Connects the family to other Lamiales while fruit/habit keeps it separate.

steps.title: 5 · Two different climbing attachments: leaf tendril versus stem rootlet
steps.photo_role: paired intact nodes, leaf petiole and tendril origin versus stem rootlets
steps.look_for: In Bignonia capreolata, trace a branched tendril back to the terminal position of a two-leaflet LEAF; in Campsis radicans, trace short aerial rootlets to the STEM. Do not infer attachment from an isolated tendril tip.
steps.why_it_matters: Separates the two local woody climbing genera even without flowers.

steps.title: 6 · Broad-leaved Catalpa versus narrow-leaved Chilopsis
steps.photo_role: matched leaf/node and fruit side-by-side, with scale
steps.look_for: Catalpa: broad simple cordate leaves, commonly opposite/whorled. Chilopsis: extremely narrow simple leaves, alternate or opposite. Both have long capsules, unlike true willows with catkins and different capsules/seeds.
steps.why_it_matters: Prevents treating all Bignoniaceae as opposite-leaved vines or mistaking desert willow for Salix.

steps.title: 7 · Tecoma door: shrub with pinnate leaves
steps.photo_role: complete Tecoma leaf at node plus flower interior and mature capsule
steps.look_for: Self-supporting shrub with pinnate leaves and a bilaterally symmetric fused corolla; confirm two-valved capsule and seed structure rather than flower color. Do not treat Campsis aerial-rootlet climbing as family-wide.
steps.why_it_matters: Routes the fifth Master Pool genus without inventing a vine habit.

comparisons.title: Bignoniaceae vs Plantaginaceae
comparisons.rule: Both can have bilabiate tubular flowers. Bignoniaceae is commonly woody with long capsules and flat winged seeds; local Penstemon is herbaceous with a smaller ordinary many-seeded capsule.

comparisons.title: Bignoniaceae vs Oleaceae
comparisons.rule: Both can be opposite-leaved woody plants; Oleaceae has tiny flowers and samara/drupe fruit rather than huge trumpet flowers and winged-seed capsules.

comparisons.title: Bignoniaceae vs Paulowniaceae
comparisons.rule: Both may have large tubular flowers and broad opposite leaves. Compare mature fruit: Catalpa has long narrow capsules, whereas Paulownia has rounded woody capsules with many tiny winged seeds. Flower color alone is unreliable.

visual_lesson.caveat: Flower shape alone is not enough; woody architecture and fruit/seed structure are the safest local confirmation.

project_pool_genus_roadmap.source: Live Master Plant Pool checked 2026-10-15; five genera, seven source rows including Tecoma stans var. angustata (not counted as a sixth genus). No species installation or synonym decision.

genera.route: Climbing vine; each leaf has two leaflets and a terminal leaf-derived branched adhesive tendril. Follow the tendril to its leaf, not the stem.
Climbing vine; opposite odd-pinnate leaves with serrated leaflets; climbs using adventitious stem-borne aerial rootlets, not leaf tendrils.
Tree with broad simple often cordate leaves, opposite or whorled; inspect long slender capsules and winged seeds rather than calling any heart-shaped leaf Catalpa.
genera.media_status: No newly verified family anatomy photo

genera.route: Shrub/small tree with exceptionally narrow simple leaves; leaf arrangement may be alternate or opposite; inspect long capsules with fringed seeds, not willow catkins.
Shrub with pinnate compound leaves, typically serrated leaflets and trumpet flowers; distinguish from Campsis by self-supporting habit and lack of aerial-rootlet climbing.
genera.caution: Varietal source row is not a separate genus or a second genus-route card.

visual_targets.formal_structure: leaf-derived tendril versus adventitious aerial rootlet
visual_targets.photo_role: matched attached nodes showing the leaf/tendril junction versus stem rootlets
visual_targets.existing_media_note: Bignonia installed flowering-habit face does not document tendril attachment; Campsis installed compound-leaf photo does not document rootlet attachment.
visual_targets.annotation_target: leaf terminal tendril insertion and stem rootlet origin

visual_targets.formal_structure: pinnately compound versus simple leaf and phyllotaxy
visual_targets.plain_language: one leaf or several leaflets; where leaves meet the stem
visual_targets.photo_role: complete leaves with nodes and scale; opposite/whorled/alternate variation
visual_targets.annotation_target: petiole, leaflets, node and leaf arrangement

visual_targets.plain_language: two longer and two shorter pollen-bearing stamens; sometimes a reduced fifth
visual_targets.photo_role: open flower throat/dissection with stamens exposed
visual_targets.annotation_target: two long, two short stamens and staminode if actually present
visual_targets.caution: Do not claim a staminode is universal or visible in the existing habit photographs.

visual_targets.formal_structure: bivalved capsule and flattened winged/fringed seeds
visual_targets.plain_language: long dry pod that splits in two and releases thin seeds
visual_targets.comparison: Bignoniaceae versus Paulowniaceae rounded woody capsule and Oleaceae samara/drupe
visual_targets.photo_role: mature opened capsule and individual seeds with ruler
visual_targets.annotation_target: two valves, placenta, seed wing or hair fringe
